definitions.explanation: Suffix attached to a noun to form a word naming a category of physical objects or substances. Common in formal, technical, and legal vocabulary.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}は{構造|こうぞう}{物|ぶつ}の{一種|いっしゅ}だ。
examples.english: A building is a type of structure.

examples.japanese: {危険|きけん}{物|ぶつ}を{機内|きない}に{持|も}ち{込|こ}んではいけない。
examples.english: You must not bring dangerous items on board.

examples.japanese: {化学|かがく}{物|ぶっ}{質|しつ}を{扱|あつか}うときは{保護|ほご}{具|ぐ}を{身|み}に{付|つ}けてください。
examples.english: When handling chemical substances, please wear protective equipment.

notes:
Suffix forming nouns that name categories of physical objects or substances. Reads ぶつ in most compounds and ぶっ before a voiceless consonant. Distinct from the same kanji read もの (an everyday word for 'thing') and from the reading もつ in expressions like {荷物|にもつ}.

COMPOUNDS:
- {建造|けんぞう}{物|ぶつ}: a building; constructed object
- {構造|こうぞう}{物|ぶつ}: a structure (engineering)
- {危険|きけん}{物|ぶつ}: dangerous item
- {化合|かごう}{物|ぶつ}: chemical compound
- {農産|のうさん}{物|ぶつ}: agricultural produce
- {汚染|おせん}{物|ぶつ}{質|しつ}: pollutant

READING DISTINCTION:
- {物|もの}: thing (everyday vocabulary; stand-alone noun)
- 〜{物|ぶつ}: object; substance (technical/formal compounds)
- 〜{物|もつ}: belongings ({荷|に}{物|もつ} luggage, {手|て}{荷|に}{物|もつ} hand baggage)
